subject: EdgeWave — Throughput choke: elevated 5xx/429 and timeouts (exec attention)
messages:
From: maya.kline@edgewave.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: adrian.chu@edgewave.com
Date: 2028-01-18T09:13:00-08:00
Subject: Spike in 5xx/429, affecting midweek batch jobs

Marissa --

We started seeing a sustained increase in 5xx and 429 responses on Monday evening that peaked overnight. Batch inference jobs (long-running streaming sessions) are timing out at higher rates, and our user-facing QPS dropped by ~30% between 23:00 and 03:00 PST. Attached is a snapshot from our metrics pipeline (capacity-graphs-qps-20280121.png).

We escalated to your support queue earlier but were told an ops lead would reach out; can we get immediate help? This is impacting our ingestion pipeline and scheduled customer deliveries tomorrow.

Highlights:
- Elevated 5xx/429 between 22:00-04:00 PST (see graph)
- Timeouts on long streaming sessions after ~25s
- Increased client-side retries causing queue backlog

We need a short-term mitigation (fallback model or rate-limiting guidance) and a timeline for root cause.

Thanks,
Maya Kline
EdgeWave — Platform Ops
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: maya.kline@edgewave.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2028-01-18T09:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429, affecting midweek batch jobs

Maya —

Thanks for the heads up and the graph. Apologies for the disruption. Ben (oncall infra) and Laura (account lead) are looped. Short answers up front:
- We are seeing a correlated autoscaling lag and node drain events in the dedicated pool serving your account overnight. That produced a temporary capacity shortfall and a retry amplification loop.
- Immediate mitigation: Ben will open a fallback route to a slightly lower-cost model variant (quantized 8-bit) with reserved capacity to reduce timeouts while we stabilize.

Ben, Laura — please provide ETA for the fallback route and a short blast-radius mitigation we can apply ASAP. Maya, we'll also propose a temporary token-rate cap to smooth retries.

Marissa
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, maya.kline@edgewave.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2028-01-18T10:06:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429, affecting midweek batch jobs

Maya / team —

I've pulled the node logs for the dedicated pool assigned to EdgeWave. Summary:
- Overnight maintenance window triggered extra node recycling in the region; concurrent with higher-than-normal batch QPS from EdgeWave (unexpected spike).
- Autoscaler took ~7m to provision replacement capacity due to GPU allocation fragmentation (several large reservations were active).
- Client retries (exponential backoff but aggressive) caused queue saturation at the front-end LB, escalating 500s and 429s.

Immediate actions I pushed at 09:50 PST:
- Opened a fallback route to the quantized model (model-redwood-q8b) with a reserved 60% throughput cap for EdgeWave (effective now).
- Applied a short-term per-API-key soft rate-limit to smooth spikes (reduces burst by 40%).
- Kicked a rolling-restart of a subset of nodes to rehydrate KV caches (ETA 12m).

Result: observed error rate drop from 18% -> 5% in the first 10 minutes. I'm continuing to monitor.

Ben Carter
SRE — Redwood Inference
From: maya.kline@edgewave.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com

2) We'd like to understand why autoscaling couldn't allocate faster — is there capacity fragmentation we should be aware of?

Adrian (CTO) is included; if this persists we'll need an exec-level update.

Maya

Subject: Executive summary: EdgeWave throughput choke — incident brief and next steps

Team / EdgeWave execs —

Attached: capacity-graphs-qps-20280121.png, hsoc2-audit-request.pdf (customer-sent).

Executive summary (for leadership):
- Incident window: 2028-01-18 22:10 PST — 2028-01-19 03:45 PST (peak errors 22:40 PST).
- Impact: short-lived but high-severity — sustained 5xx/429 spike; observed 30% drop in successful QPS for customer streaming jobs; several scheduled batch jobs retried and delayed.
- Root cause (short): autoscaler lag due to GPU allocation fragmentation during an overlapping maintenance/recycle window, amplified by aggressive client-side retries causing queue saturation.
- Short-term mitigations applied: fallback to q8b model with reserved capacity, soft per-key rate limiting, targeted node restarts to rehydrate caches. Error-rate reduced to ~4–6% within 15 minutes.
- Recommended customer-facing next steps:
  1) Joint postmortem and capacity planning session (pick a date)
  2) Recommend EdgeWave adopt exponential backoff with jitter and a capped retry policy for long streaming sessions (we can provide a sample middleware snippet)
  3) Offer a one-time billing credit for the incident window and a 2-week elevated-support window.

Action items:
- Marissa: approve compensation approach and draft customer-facing exec note.
- Ben: provide a technical RCA draft (INF-2371) with logs and autoscaler timeline.
- Laura/Stephanie: coordinate the postmortem and client communication.

Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Customer Success Operations — Redwood Inference
